operations.old: 0.1 Since $k>1$, [F10] and [F20] give $\log k>\log1=0$, and [F9] makes $\log k$ a real number; hence the specified $\eta$ is a positive finite real, as required by the procedure. Initially $\widehat S_{0,i}=0$ is finite for every $i$ by [F18]. Suppose all $\widehat S_{t-1,i}$ are finite. Then each $\exp(\eta\widehat S_{t-1,i})$ is a positive finite real by [F7] and the real-valued exponential definition [F17]. Its finite sum over $[k]$ is positive and finite, so [F1] gives $P_{t,i}>0$ and $\sum_iP_{t,i}=1$. The assumed measurable action draw exists by [F21]; its observed reward is in $[0,1]$. Thus each $\widehat Y_{t,i}=\mathbf1\{A_t=i\}(1-X_t)/P_{t,i}$ and $\widehat X_{t,i}=1-\widehat Y_{t,i}$ is finite, and [F19] makes every $\widehat S_{t,i}$ finite. Induction proves these facts through round $n$. The prescribed loop has the finite index set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and each round consists of the finite operations just checked together with an assumed draw, so it completes exactly $n$ rounds. operations.new: 0.1 First fix any positive finite real learning rate $\eta$ and any reward sequence admitted by the algorithm. Initially $\widehat S_{0,i}=0$ is finite for every $i$ by [F18]. Suppose all $\widehat S_{t-1,i}$ are finite. Then each $\exp(\eta\widehat S_{t-1,i})$ is a positive finite real by [F7] and the real-valued exponential definition [F17]. Its finite sum over $[k]$ is positive and finite, so [F1] gives $P_{t,i}>0$ and $\sum_iP_{t,i}=1$. The assumed measurable action draw exists by [F21]; its observed reward is in $[0,1]$. Thus each $\widehat Y_{t,i}=\mathbf1\{A_t=i\}(1-X_t)/P_{t,i}$ and $\widehat X_{t,i}=1-\widehat Y_{t,i}$ is finite, and [F19] makes every $\widehat S_{t,i}$ finite. Induction proves these facts through round $n$. The prescribed loop has the finite index set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and each round consists of the finite operations just checked together with an assumed draw, so it completes exactly $n$ rounds. This argument uses only $\eta>0$ and the algorithm's reward range, for either fixed or deterministic past-adaptive rewards. For the rate in the regret clauses, $k>1$, [F10] and [F20] give $\log k>\log1=0$, and [F9] makes $\log k$ real; hence that tuned $\eta$ is also a positive finite real and the same argument applies to it. [given, F1, F7, F9, F10, F17, F18, F19, F20, F21, induction]
